_comment: sui's `builtins` registry, PINNED — the drift gate for the builtin surface.
WHY. sui's registry WAS a strict SUPERSET of CppNix's, and nothing noticed.
Measured 2026-08-17 against nix 2.31.5: the sui-eval tree-walker exposed 126
names to nix's 118, with ZERO absent — containment in exactly the wrong
direction. The consequence is a correctness defect with a very quiet
signature: an expression using one of the extra names MUST fail on real nix
(`error: attribute 'filterAttrs' missing`) and SUCCEEDED on sui. That is not
a missing feature — it is sui accepting a program nix rejects, which is the
one direction a compatibility layer must never drift in. Found by
`diff_filter_attrs`, which had been gated off behind SUI_TEST_ONLINE and
therefore never ran.
★ THE SIX LEAKS ARE NOW REMOVED (2026-08-17, same day as the finding).
concatStrings, filterAttrs, hasPrefix, hasSuffix, toLower and toUpper are
gone from ALL THREE engines — the sui-eval tree-walker, the sui-bytecode VM,
and sui-ir's `eval_ir`. Measured after removal:
tree-walker (sui-eval, the default engine)   120
bytecode VM (sui-bytecode, `sui eval --vm`)  122
eval_ir     (sui-ir, shadow-only)            120
The walker and eval_ir AGREE exactly (`sui-ir/tests/eval_differential.rs`
`builtins_registry_parity` byte-compares the two key lists). The VM still
carries 2 names neither of the others has — see `cli_divergence` — and those
2 are a SEPARATE, still-open instance of this same defect class, recorded
below rather than quietly folded into the fixed count.
★ AND THE REGISTRY IS NOT ONE REGISTRY. Found the same day, by this gate's
own first red run: `sui eval --json -E 'builtins.attrNames builtins'` did
NOT return the walker's set, and the difference was BIDIRECTIONAL — neither
was a superset of the other. `builtins.path` and the `builtins.builtins`
self-reference existed for a library consumer and NOT for anyone typing
`sui eval`. Two evaluators, two languages, one binary name. This is the same
shape as the four disjoint path-redirect namespaces already recorded in this
repo, and it is the more serious half of what this file documents — a
superset is a permissiveness bug, but a split registry means the answer
depends on which door you came through. The split narrowed from 10 names to
6 when the VM's builtin fixes landed, and to 6 again after this removal
(which took 6 names off BOTH sides and so left the delta unchanged).
THE THREE CLASSES ARE NOT THE SAME DEFECT, and the split was measured with
`--extra-experimental-features`, not assumed. Re-measured 2026-08-17: nix
2.31.5 exposes 118 names by default and 120 with every experimental feature
on, the two extra being `fetchClosure` and `outputOf`. The 120-name
all-features set is the oracle the classification below is judged against —
judging a lib leak against the 118-name default set would conflate it with
the experimental class, which is the whole distinction:
experimental — a REAL CppNix builtin, merely gated behind an experimental
feature flag. `builtins ? fetchClosure` is false on a default nix and
true with `fetch-closure` enabled. Exposing one unconditionally is a
feature-gating divergence, not an invented builtin. Low severity. Empty
for the walker — both instances (fetchClosure, outputOf) are VM-side.
nixpkgs_lib_leak — NOT a language builtin at any feature level. These are
nixpkgs `lib` functions (lib.filterAttrs, lib.strings.hasPrefix, …) that
were implemented into `builtins` instead of left to nixpkgs. Every one
verified absent from nix with ALL experimental features enabled. This
was the real defect class; it is now EMPTY for the walker, and the six
names it held are recorded in `removed_nixpkgs_lib_leaks` as a
shrink-only ratchet so they cannot come back quietly.
sui_extension — deliberate, sui-specific, and namespaced as such
(`builtins.sui`, `builtins.resolveFlakeRef`). Divergence by design, not
by accident. Kept as its own class so a future leak cannot be filed here
to make the leak count go down.
WHY THE REMOVAL COSTS NOTHING A NIX PROGRAM COULD LEGALLY DO. Each of the
six is implemented in nixpkgs' own `lib`, which never routes through
`builtins` — so `lib.filterAttrs` and friends keep working unchanged. The
one name with a real-nix equivalent is `concatStrings`, which is exactly
`concatStringsSep ""`; both engines have that, nix has it, and the
empty-separator context-accumulation path stays covered by the parity corpus
row "concatStringsSep empty-sep single-element context", which was
deliberately written through `concatStringsSep ""` for this exact reason.
AND THE REASON `filterAttrs` WAS THE WORST OF THE SIX: nixpkgs
feature-detects with `builtins ? filterAttrs`. sui exposing it did not merely
accept an extra expression — it silently steered nixpkgs down a DIFFERENT
branch than real nix takes. A permissiveness bug that changes which code runs
is not a superset, it is a fork.
THE OTHER DIRECTION for the walker is 2 names, both experimental-gated:
`fetchClosure` and `outputOf` are in nix-with-flags and not in the walker.
They are absences, not overreach — the safe direction — and are not gated
here. `pending-builtin-registry: walker lacks fetchClosure + outputOf`
HOW THIS GATE WORKS. The offline half always runs and is total: sui's live
registry must equal `sui_registry` exactly, so ADDING or REMOVING any
builtin is red until this file moves in the same commit. Because that pin is
deliberately MOVABLE (that is the point — it moves in the same commit), it
is on its own too weak to keep a removed leak removed: re-adding one to both
the code and the pin would go green. `removed_nixpkgs_lib_leaks` closes that
hole as a ratchet the offline half enforces — the list may GROW and may
never SHRINK. The online half (SUI_TEST_ONLINE=1) additionally re-derives
the classification against the host's nix, so a name silently changing class
is caught too.
Gate: tests/builtin_registry.rs.
Partitions the walker's names that real nix does not have. Verified with
--extra-experimental-features so `experimental` and `nixpkgs_lib_leak`
are separated by measurement, not by guess. BOTH are empty for the
walker today: the two feature-gated builtins (fetchClosure, outputOf)
exist only on the VM side, and the six lib leaks were removed
2026-08-17. They are kept as declared, empty arms so a newly-added name
has an obvious home rather than being mislabelled — and note that an
empty arm here is NOT a vacuous gate: the online totality check below
still requires the union of all three arms to equal sui's extras
exactly, so a new unclassified extra is red whether or not any arm is
empty.
The shrink-only ratchet. Every name here was once in `builtins`, was
measured absent from nix 2.31.5 with ALL experimental features enabled,
and was removed on 2026-08-17. `removed_lib_leaks_stay_removed` asserts
none of them is live.
This list may GROW and may NEVER SHRINK. Shrinking it is precisely how a
resurrected leak would be made to pass, so the gate floors its length
BEFORE comparing anything and carries that length into the compared
value.
`names` is a flat array on purpose — the gate's `names()` reader panics
on a missing field rather than defaulting to the empty set, so a typo in
the path is red rather than vacuously green.
Measured, not gated by THIS file — the offline test reads the walker
in-process, and pinning the VM's set from here would mean spawning a
binary that may not be built when the test runs. The VM's own crate now
carries the in-process half instead: `sui-bytecode`'s
`vm_has_no_nixpkgs_lib_leaks` asserts the six are absent there without
spawning anything.
Re-measured 2026-08-17 AFTER the six-leak removal, against the binary
built from this tree:
sui eval       --json -E 'builtins.attrNames builtins'   # walker, 120
sui eval --vm  --json -E 'builtins.attrNames builtins'   # VM,     122
★ `isStorePath` and `toInt` are a STILL-OPEN instance of the same defect
class this file exists for: both were measured absent from nix 2.31.5
with every experimental feature on, so they are nixpkgs `lib` leaks too
(lib.isStorePath, lib.strings.toInt) — they are simply VM-only, and
removing them was out of scope for the six-name change. They are named
here rather than left inside a bare count, because a count is exactly
where this class hides.
`pending-builtin-registry: drop isStorePath + toInt from the VM`
